_about: LGIC_LGCTFM round 4, cell LT-m-1 (TO-LT-m-1-r4), filed by 0.9.0_WK_LGIC_LGCTFM~2. The record shape is quoted from the ONE carrier, org/missions/D14/LGIC/LGIC_LGCTFM/deliverables/2.0.0_SA_COO~G/fixed_inputs/r4/R4_BASE.json (LGIC_ENFORCE-S85). This cell fills the `entry` and `stale_proofs` blocks ONLY; `repoint`, `coverage_delta` and `run` belong to the cells on slot ~1 and are deliberately absent rather than stubbed.

entry.canonical_call: comp-find --corpus aws '<name-or-arn pattern>' [NODE_TYPE ...] [--all | --page N] [--budget N]   # pathspecs ARE node_type filters (LAMBDA, IAM_ROLE, S3_BUCKET, ...); --name '<glob>' matches name/arn only; --cursor resumes a budget-stopped pull
entry.status_claim: measured -- the manifest's own per-entry schema (org/modules/graph/graph-call-manifest.yaml:29 at HEAD) enumerates canonical|deprecated|planned|retired, 125 of the 128 pre-existing entries carry `canonical`, and NFRA_GRAPHS s.7 AC1 -- the bar R-81 quotes to justify this entry -- reads 'exactly one CANONICAL entry per distinct graph use-case'. The round-4 checker's m1-entry arm requires status in (active|current|live), which this file has never used. The divergence is filed as BLOCKING row LGIC_LGCTFM-W2-S35 and is NOT worked around by typing a token into a shared estate surface.
entry.where: org/modules/graph/graph-call-manifest.yaml, inserted immediately after cloud.lookup.nodes_by_type (its nearest neighbour) and before cloud.reachability.transitive (the RELATIONS half of the same comp-which question)
entry.why_this_instrument_and_not_my_judgment: R-81 s.3 assigns it: 'WHICH resources compose the subject -> comp-find --corpus aws', on src=full-derive 217 of 217 LAMBDA nodes, and it is the only surface already carrying the derived-vs-declared discriminator AS A FIELD. Verified live by this cell on 2026-09-19: `comp-find --corpus aws '49financial' --limit 5` printed VINTAGE (built 2026-09-19T00:55:44Z, stitch source 2026-09-18T03:01:14Z, manifest 1ba8ff79d94b), DENOMINATOR (8 hits across 2590 aws nodes scanned), a DRIFT band over every scanned node (DECLARED 1721, LIVE-no-DECLARED 341, IN_REPO 245, AWS_MANAGED 38, MULTI_STATE_MANAGED 9, LIVE-INCREMENTAL 4, unset 232) and WITHIN BUDGET 7.19s of 90s.

how_the_near_duplicate_set_was_CHOSEN.method: SUBTRACTION FROM A PRINTED DENOMINATOR, not recall (Rule 24 i). Population = the 128 pre-existing entries. Sieve, each arm's count printed: (a) layer == cloud -> 39; (b) tool == comp-find -> 1 (search.graded.find, which arm (a) does not hold because its layer is `source` -- so the tool axis is a SECOND arm, not a subset of the first); (c) of the remaining 88, the entries whose serialized text matches /aws|resource|inventory|exist|census|list/i -> 30. 39 + 1 + 30 = 70 candidates read; the 58 not read are entries matching none of the three arms. UNSCOPED CONTROL on the claim's own population: `comp-find 'corpus aws' org/modules/graph/graph-call-manifest.yaml --all` returned 0 hits across 1 file scanned -- the string `--corpus aws` appears NOWHERE in the manifest at the cut, so no pre-existing entry routes this question by any spelling and the six-way tie is a true absence rather than a duplicate.

near_duplicates_considered.why_different: THE CLOSEST, and the one a reader most plausibly mis-lands on. It lists nodes of ONE node_type YOU ALREADY NAME ('all Lambdas', 'all roles') off the served Kuzu projection via Cypher. Two differences, both structural: (1) GRAIN OF THE QUESTION -- it takes a TYPE and returns members; this entry takes a SUBJECT TOKEN (a firm, a pipeline, a product name) and returns members ACROSS types, banded by type. (2) It returns node_id and name and NOTHING ELSE -- no drift_class -- so it cannot answer 'is this live thing declared in the repo', which is the half of the inventory question R-81 built this route around (LIVE-no-DECLARED). R-81 assigns comp-kuzu the RELATIONS question, and this entry's own use_case hands relations back to it by name.

ONE resource you have ALREADY IDENTIFIED (exact ARN, exact name, or a substring that resolves to one), synthesized into what it IS and what it DOES. It is the step AFTER inventory: its input is the output of this entry. Its own anti_pattern says it is exact/lexical find of ONE resource -- it presupposes you know the resource exists, which is precisely what the inventory question asks.

THE SAME TOOL, and that is exactly why it must be named. Different CORPUS and different LAYER (source): it searches the repository working tree, so it answers 'what does the repo DECLARE'. It is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to the class this entry exists to surface -- a live resource the repo never declared (LIVE-no-DECLARED, 341 of 2590 nodes on the run above) has no repo text to match. One verb, two planes, two entries: the id namespace (search.* vs cloud.*) is the only thing that keeps the question from collapsing into the tool.

Lists the resource CLASSES the cloud compiler MODELS -- a 30-type hand list that is a CEILING on the graph (R-81 s.4 names it as an undated hand surface). Types, not instances; a schema question, not an existence question. It is also a comp-aws call.

Per-class COUNTS, drift distribution and finding totals over a derived snapshot -- an AGGREGATE. It tells you 217 Lambdas exist; it cannot tell you WHICH ones compose your subject, and you cannot act on a count. Also comp-aws (a derive).
The DELTA between two cloud-graph snapshots -- a question about CHANGE over time, with two inputs. This entry's question has one input and no time axis: what is there now.

An inventory, but scoped to ONE node_type (secrets) and carrying facets no general inventory has (rotation age, firm tagging, freshness) -- and its point is to avoid a raw get-secret-value. A type-scoped instrument with a safety purpose is not the cross-type existence route; the general route BANDS secrets as one node_type among many.

R-81's 1.55 tie entrant (comp-keys). It answers which KEYS/PARTITIONS exist under an S3 prefix -- OBJECT grain, INSIDE one bucket. This entry works at RESOURCE grain: the bucket itself is one node. The two never return the same row, and reading one for the other is a grain error, not a preference.

The same object-vs-resource grain distinction, on the OPAL_ASSETS monolith specifically: per-folder object counts, bytes, feeds and date frontier for ONE bucket's channels. A census of CONTENTS, not of resources.
Which resources have gone COLD, ranked by last invocation. It PRESUPPOSES the inventory and adds a usage axis; its question is 'which of these is dead', not 'which of these exist'.

Whether two resources do the same JOB (BM25 over the summary corpus). Presupposes the inventory and adds a purpose axis; its own anti_pattern already refuses the describe-ONE and the name/body-duplicate questions, so its boundary is drawn on the same side.
Whether a LOGICAL resource is duplicated across firms/services. A relation BETWEEN inventory rows, computed on top of the inventory.

R-81's 1.60 tie entrant (comp-iam) and the reason the tie was dangerous rather than merely untidy. It answers AUTHORIZATION -- does this role grant what this code calls. R-81 refuses comp-iam gaps/roles/services/stats as a DISCOVERY source outright: their population is the hand-maintained lambda-source-map.json and they print no plane banner and no scanned denominator, so a reader who lands here for an existence question gets an answer shaped like a census and sourced from a hand file. Authorization stays cloud.iam.simulate_exact_resource / cloud.iam.applied_plane_reconcile (live/reconcile/simulate only).

R-81's 1.52 tie entrant (comp-blast). Blast radius FROM A NODE YOU ALREADY NAME -- an edge traversal, the relations half. Its input is one node_id; this entry's output is what that input is drawn from.

R-81's 1.50 tie entrant (comp-estate). Named-thread estate traversal, and REFUSED as a resource source by R-81 on a measured basis: it answers from estate-coverage-resolver.json, generated_at 2026-08-20, last_review 2026-07-30, regeneration EXPLICITLY PARKED (CTO 2026-08-14) -- it cannot see a Lambda created since August. A parked generated file is a different EPISTEMIC object from a served plane that prints its own vintage, which is why this is a refusal in the anti_pattern rather than a neighbouring route.

The WRITE path -- comp-aws derive, an 8-minute rebuild, scheduled and not agent-default, and DEPRECATED FOR AGENT USE by Andrew-direct (NFRA_CLDGRPH CG-s-30). It is the producer of the plane this entry reads. Naming it here is the point: the tie made a derive look like a peer of a read.

How OLD is the answer -- a question about the instrument rather than about the estate. Not a duplicate but the POSTURE this entry inherits: there is no refresh an agent runs, so this entry's rebuild_trigger is `none` and points here.

What FIRES a compute resource -- R-81's own third row, assigned to comp-trigger. Named so the split is complete on the face of the file: exists (here) / relates (cloud.reachability.transitive) / fires (here) / is authorized (cloud.iam.*).

entry.tie_ended_how: R-81's tie was SIX TOOLS ON ONE QUESTION. It is not resolved by ranking them -- it is resolved by splitting the question into the four R-81 already assigns and declaring ONE entry for the half that had none. Each of the other five tied tools now lands on an entry that OWNS a different half (comp-iam -> cloud.iam.*, comp-blast -> cloud.blast.what_breaks, comp-kuzu -> cloud.reachability.transitive, comp-keys -> pipeline.keys.enumerate at object grain) or is REFUSED by name in this entry's anti_pattern with its measured reason (comp-estate, comp-routes, comp-aws, comp-iam's four report subcommands). EXACTLY ONE cloud.inventory.* entry exists: two would re-create the tie in the file meant to end it.
entry.what_this_entry_does_not_claim: That comp-find --corpus aws sees everything. Its denominator is the SERVED aws plane's node set (2590 nodes at the vintage above) and its ceiling is the cloud compiler's 30-type CLASSES list (R-81 s.4): an unmodeled service is invisible while the graph publishes clean. The entry's freshness field states the vintage line and the drift banding so a reader gets the limit with the answer; it does not assert the limit away.
